result.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is credited with teaching reasoning models to write {wait} before reconsidering a step, yet large RL accuracy gains do not require the word. This view can confuse what RL discovers with what a model inherits from its training data. We trace the word through open models' training histories, reading it with label-free indices of frequency, position, form and usage and an injected-error test, all computed from sampled outputs. We find that zero-RL almost never coins the marker: on bases that lack the word, RL raises MATH-500 accuracy substantially while {wait} stays near absent. It arrives with training data: mid-training in OLMo-3, and fine-tuning on reasoning traces installs it in most models whose base lacks it. Where the base already uses it, both released RL-Zero recipes (OLMo-3, MiMo) multiply it, whereas KL-free GRPO from the same base does not; OLMo-3's recipe wears down its form and makes it a more sensitive but more liberal alarm; RL after supervised fine-tuning barely changes it, and our GRPO recipe erases a marker seeded by fine-tuning. Finally, we show that marker frequency alone does not indicate RL-induced reasoning and caution against LLM-as-a-judge revision metrics, as automated judges can reverse human-labelled trends.

AI.brief_summary: 论文沿开源模型的训练史追踪「wait」标记的来源，用无标签的频率、位置、形式与用法指标及注入错误测试，检验该标记是训练数据带来的还是 RL 发现的。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「行为归因于数据继承还是训练信号」的追踪范式与注入错误诊断，可能可供核查 LVR 中回看视觉证据、停止等 latent 推理行为究竟源自监督数据还是训练目标。
